svg.aria-label: M-S-DROP: from tick 400 every message on the bus is dropped at delivery. Experts still decide, by rule or through CrewAI and Ollama, but every decision is applied by a message, so nothing reaches the sub-agents, the other experts or the robots. Arrivals and vans run outside the bus. Seed 11, rules only: last parcel out at 583, collapse at 722, dock full at 1141; DK-RMM DEVIATING at 401, UNSTABLE at 421, RCT at 461.
svg.text: M-S-DROP: from tick 400 every message on the bus is dropped at delivery, and CrewAI with it
Normal configuration for ticks 0 to 399. At tick 400 CollapseFaults sets MessageBus.delay_rule = DropAll(); nothing ever removes it. Every expert answers by its Python
rule first and consults CrewAI (qwen3:8b on local Ollama) only when the rule is insufficient. Nothing in the agents, the bus code, CrewAI or DK-RMM is changed by the scenario.

svg.text: Decisions still compute: experts read the floor directly, not by message.
the only way an agent reaches another agent or a robot
send(): writes a message event (DK-RMM counts it
as attempted) and queues the message in _pending
deliver(), at the start of the next tick, asks

SUBTASK_REQUEST and SUBTASK_RESULT
TASK_ASSIGNMENT

svg.text: never receive a SUBTASK_REQUEST, so never answer; the
experts keep asking, so attempted traffic stays near Normal
while delivered traffic falls to zero
ROUTE_RESPONSE: each runs on what it already knows
RobotAgent acts only on a delivered ROBOT_COMMAND, and none
arrives: each finishes the errand it already had, then stands
idle. In the rules-only campaign 2 to 4 robots stood idle and
available to the end, and the 4 charge points went unused.
The CONSULT_* messages record a consultation that has
already run in-process through the CrewAI tool, so dropping
them changes no answer. What the drop takes from CrewAI is
its effect: the decision it reaches is applied by a message,
and that message is dropped like every other.
Outside the bus, so untouched by the fault

g.text: Arrivals
The generator keeps putting parcels on the intake dock
(about 1 per 40 ticks); past the dock limit they are refused.
Van timetable
Vans keep leaving on schedule, carrying only parcels
that were already at the dispatch door.
DK-RMM
Reads the event log from outside: message (attempted)
against message_dropped gives the failure rate.

svg.text: Seeds 12 to 15, rules only: all COLLAPSED, at tick 666 to 708

g.text: A model call goes to Ollama over HTTP, not the bus,
and is logged as an llm_call event.
Owner and peer talk through a CrewAI tool, in-process,
so the consultation completes and a DECISION is parsed.
The PolicyGate still checks every answer.
Sub-agents' answers never arrive, so an expert decides
from its own direct reads of the floor.
Whatever it chooses, by rule or by model, is applied by a
message, and the message is dropped: the choice is a
decision event with no effect on the robots or the parcels.
Panel 2 is rules only: the collapse campaign (seeds 11
to 15) and the DK-RMM validation run (seed 11).
No model-mode M-S-DROP run exists yet, so the CrewAI
path in panels 1 and 3 is read from the code, not from a
run. How often the rules hand over to the model under the
drop is not known until that run is made.
